notes:
K8Secret 0.6.12 — diagnostics that can answer this.

This release does not claim to fix the connection problem some of you are seeing. It makes the app able to prove what is actually happening, on the machine where it happens, rather than being diagnosed by inference from one where it doesn't.

Run macos/scripts/diagnose.sh from the repository, or set K8SECRET_TLS_DEBUG=1 when launching the app from a terminal, and the trace now includes the TLS version and cipher the two ends actually negotiated, whether the handshake completed at all, your client certificate's subject and expiry date, which credentials the context carries, and whether K8Secret capped the TLS version. The diagnostic also asks your API server directly — with openssl, nothing to do with the app — whether it requests a client certificate at TLS 1.2 and at TLS 1.3, which is the question that distinguishes most of the causes.

You can also override the cap that 0.6.11 introduced, with K8SECRET_TLS_MAX=1.3 or 1.2, so it can be tested both ways rather than taken on faith.
